Wikipedia: Kollwitz among the artists who embraced social realism

highlight.text: Social realism is work produced by painters, printmakers, photographers, writers, filmmakers and some musicians that aims to draw attention to the real socio-political conditions of the working class as a means to critique the power structures behind these conditions.

work.text: In 1924 she finished her three most famous posters: Germany's Children Starving, Bread, and Never Again War ("Nie Wieder Krieg").

moment.text: The drawings and prints of Kathe Kollwitz are too fervent and sincere to be classed as propaganda; they … are the expression of suffering and anguish, and of the joys and desires of the German workers.
moment.lead: An American museum introducing her prints in 1933:

source.author: Worcester Art Museum
source.title: Exhibition of Prints by Käthe Kollwitz: Studies from the German Revolution, 1919–21 (catalogue introduction, signed F.H.T.)

moment.text: Artists in Western Europe also embraced social realism in the early 20th century, including … German artists Käthe Kollwitz, George Grosz, Otto Dix, and Max Beckmann

matters.text: My work is not, of course, pure art in the sense that Schmidt-Rottluff's is, but it is art nonetheless... It is all right with me that my work serves a purpose. I want to have an effect on my time, in which human beings are so confused and in need of help.

source.author: Käthe Kollwitz
source.title: Quoted in Renate Hinz, Käthe Kollwitz: Graphics, Posters, Drawings (1981), introduction, p. xxiii, quoted on Wikiquote

matters.text: There must be understanding between the artist and the people. In the best ages of art that has always been the case.

source.author: Käthe Kollwitz
